scope: Final RTL-only commit candidate; unrelated working-tree changes are excluded.
lineEndings: Raw benchmark hashes identify the frozen Windows files. Staged Git blobs were verified equal after CRLF-to-LF normalization; canonicalLfSources identifies those blobs with SHA-256.

priority.methodology: Alternating paired, sequential workloads in real Chromium with full frozen extensions. One live edit after history scanning starts; separately, activation on a long chat scrolled to its last viewport. Native DOM and text costs, no artificial per-node delay.
limitations: Synthetic site markup does not prove live-site compatibility.
Priority latency is a direction-write timestamp, not keyboard-to-paint latency.
Scan CPU covers instrumented iterator tasks; viewport hit testing and queue preparation preceding the first iterator are not included.
Complete elapsed time includes source activation and renderer scheduling and is reported separately from priority latency.

regression.methodology: Alternating paired runs in actual Chromium with the full extension. One workload is measured at a time. No simulated processing delay or CPU cost. Other optional extension tools are disabled. Both immutable snapshots use identical fixture, instrumentation and source hashes. Medians are reported separately for initial activation, lazy insertion, normal streaming and three formatted token-burst workloads.
limitations: Synthetic fixtures do not guarantee equivalent speedups on every live site.
Elapsed streaming includes fixed animation-frame pacing; CPU time is a separate metric.
Renderer frame gaps include native DOM layout, text shaping and rendering, not only extension work.
Synthetic input dispatch exercises the actual direction handler but is not a physical keyboard-to-paint latency measurement.
